paper.purpose: The default surface for every route. bg-paper. 36 uses.

ink.purpose: Primary text and black fill. The most-used token on the site (129 uses). 19.80:1 on paper.

ink-2.purpose: Secondary and body copy (55 uses). 8.86:1 on paper — clears AAA.

ink-3.purpose: Tertiary, meta and muted labels (69 uses). 4.81:1 on paper, 4.61:1 on fill — clears AA at the 10-13px sizes it is actually used at. Superseded #8a8a8a (3.45:1), which failed.

line.purpose: The site's only divider and card border (59 uses). Always 1px.

line-2.purpose: Stronger hairline reserved for form controls, so inputs read as inputs (27 uses).

fill.purpose: The ONE raised step (23 uses). Never invent a grey between paper and fill.

error.purpose: Validation and error text; also the weak-spot callout tint at 6% alpha.

accent.purpose: Data-viz lane A / primary curve. Chart geometry ONLY — never chrome.

accent-2.purpose: Data-viz lane B, dashed so lanes differ by colour AND dash, not hue alone. 3.72:1 — fails AA as text; graphics only.

title.purpose: NO DEDICATED TOKEN. Filled in practice by `text-ui font-medium` (15px / -0.01em / 500). A real gap in the scale.

body.purpose: Running copy. 16px / 1.5. Token: --text-body. Cap measure at 58-65ch.

label.purpose: Labels, captions, numeric read-outs. 13px / 1.5. Token: --text-meta. Uppercase tracked 0.1-0.12em at 10-11px; numbers get tabular-nums, never a monospace face.

wordmark.purpose: The 'soma' wordmark only. 23px / 1 / -0.01em / 500. Token: --text-wordmark. One use site-wide (SiteHeader).

shadows.name: overlay
shadows.purpose: The ONLY true drop shadow in src/. Modal/dialog panels exclusively (UploadDialog). Flat surfaces get a hairline instead — never a shadow.

shadows.name: scrim
shadows.purpose: Full-viewport dim behind a modal. Not elevation; occlusion.

shadows.name: thumb-knockout
shadows.purpose: A paper ring that lets the scrubber thumb read against both the ink fill and the track. A knockout, not a shadow.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: The system's established focus treatment (globals.css:159). Apply to every interactive control.

motion.name: default
motion.purpose: Tailwind v4's inherited default. 28 of the site's 30 transitions declare no duration or easing and land here — the effective house curve, though never written down.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Explicit ease-out, used on the upload progress bar.

motion.name: story-ease
motion.purpose: The standalone /story walkthrough's reveal curve (public/story.html --ease). Not shared with the app.

motion.name: hover-lift
motion.purpose: The only permitted interactive lift. There is no shadow-based hover state anywhere.

breakpoints.name: md
breakpoints.purpose: The only structural breakpoint that carries real layout weight — the /demo read-out grid collapses below it (md:grid-cols-[300px_1fr]).

breakpoints.name: sm
breakpoints.purpose: Used sparingly for inline type and spacing adjustments.

components.name: Serif-Italic Accent
components.description: The system's one expressive gesture: exactly ONE serif-italic word per view, on the emotional word, inside an otherwise medium-weight sans heading.

narrative.overview:
Swiss/editorial minimalism where restraint is the argument. The surface is near-monochrome by conviction, not by timidity: a seven-step achromatic ramp carries one hundred percent of the interface, and the single muted slate/teal pair is held in reserve for readings — chart geometry only, never chrome. Depth is drawn, not lit. In the whole application there is exactly one true drop shadow, and it belongs to the modal; every other surface separates by a one-pixel hairline and a four-percent step from paper to fill.

The expressive budget is spent once per view, on a single serif-italic word inside an otherwise medium-weight sans heading. That one gesture is the whole personality — a term set down by hand in an otherwise typeset page. Everything else is calibrated: tabular figures, uppercase tracked labels, no monospace anywhere, and geometry that resolves its colours from the same tokens the interface uses.

The name holds three readings at once. Calibrated, because restraint here is precision rather than reticence, and nothing uncalibrated is admitted to the surface. Record, because the page is a notebook that writes down what actually happened. And under the current product thesis, Record carries a third sense: the corpus itself, growing one ad at a time.
keyCharacteristics: Near-monochrome: a 7-step achromatic ramp carries the entire UI
One reserved accent pair, admitted to charts and nothing else
Depth by hairline and a single 4% surface step — not by shadow
Exactly one serif-italic accent word per view
Tabular figures and uppercase tracked labels; no monospace anywhere
Light-only — there is no dark mode, verified across the entire repo
Calm, short, ease-out motion; every 3D surface holds a static pose under reduced-motion

rules.name: The Data-Only Accent Rule
rules.body: --color-accent and --color-accent-2 are admitted to chart geometry and nothing else. Never a button, link, heading, bullet, or checkmark. At 3.72:1, accent-2 is not a legal text colour.

rules.name: The Single Raised Step Rule
rules.body: There is exactly one step above paper, and it is fill (#fafafa). Do not invent a grey in between.

rules.name: The One Accent Word Rule
rules.body: Exactly one serif-italic word per view, on the emotional word. Nothing else is italicised, and a second accent is never added.

rules.name: The No-Monospace Rule
rules.body: There is no monospace anywhere, the /demo data tool included. Numbers are sans with tabular-nums — digits that align without a monospace face. This applies to canvas ctx.font strings and SVG font-family attributes too, where a grep for className will never find them.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Flat surfaces get a 1px hairline, never a shadow and never a glow. The one permitted drop shadow belongs to overlays. Interactive lift is a 2px translate or a 1.02 scale — never a shadow bloom.

rules.name: The Fenced Decoration Rule
rules.body: Decorative geometry and model output are visually separable, and decoration is labelled as such. Decoration never borrows the accent reserved for real readings.

dos: Do use semantic tokens (text-ink-2, bg-fill, border-line).
Do keep one serif-italic accent word per view.
Do set labels + numbers in uppercase tracked sans (numbers tabular-nums).
Do show attention, language load, and the lit cortical profile publicly.
Do keep accent / accent-2 inside charts.
Do leave the hero (Landing.tsx / Brain.tsx) untouched.
donts: Don't paste #4a4a4a / #fafafa / #e2e2e2 — a token covers it.
Don't italicise anything else or add a second accent.
Don't reach for font-mono — labels are uppercase tracked sans.
Don't surface valence / arousal (emotion) on /demo or /story — it's private research.
Don't use accent / accent-2 for buttons, links, or headings.
Don't add shadows to flat surfaces or glows to curves.
Don't invent greys between paper and fill.
